articles.title: Putin, Saudi crown prince discuss safe passage through Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb
articles.summary: Middle East News: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman discussed the need to ensure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and.
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman discussed the need to ensure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb during a phone call on Tuesday, the Kremlin said, as disruptions to the key waterways continue to affect regional oil flows and global trade.The two leaders exchanged views on the situation in the Middle East and stressed that a political and diplomatic settlement remained the only viable path forward, according to the Kremlin.They also "underscored the need for a swift cessation of hostilities" in Yemen amid the deteriorating military and political situation there.Kremlin stresses need to keep key waterways open"The importance of ensuring the safe and unimpeded passage of vessels through the region's international waterways, including the Bab el-Mandeb and Strait of Hormuz, was emphasised," the Kremlin said, as quoted by Reuters.The two waterways are important routes for global energy shipments. With the Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb routes disrupted by Iran and Iran-allied Houthi militants, Saudi Arabia has been forced to use Egypt's Suez Canal to export oil.The United States, which bombed the Houthis for two months last year, has so far rejected repeated requests from Mohammed bin Salman to rejoin the fight against the group.The New York Times reported that US President Donald Trump called off US strikes against the Houthis on Sunday at the last minute, after troops had already begun loading bombs onto planes.Saudi oil exports rise as Red Sea risks persistSaudi Arabia's crude oil exports rose about 3.3% in July from the previous month to 4.125 million barrels per day, their highest level since March, according to Joint Organizations Data Initiative data reported by Reuters.Saudi crude production also increased to 8.135 million barrels per day in July from 7.122 million bpd in June."Saudi crude and product exports increased in July as regional tensions moderated," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said, while warning that exports could be weaker in August, particularly from Red Sea terminals, because of renewed tensions involving the Houthis.Saudi refinery crude throughput fell slightly to 2.478 million bpd in July from 2.498 million bpd in June.Saudi Arabia also resumed operations at its East-West Pipeline, with exports potentially following from the Red Sea port of Yanbu, according to three sources cited by Reuters. Drone attacks had forced the kingdom to shut the pipeline on September 13.Iran says Hormuz could reopen within seven daysA senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade on Iranian ports.Meanwhile, Houthi fighters pushed to seize strategic heights in Yemen on Monday in an effort to cut off the Red Sea coast from areas held by Saudi-backed forces.The developments come as the security situation around the region's key shipping routes remains closely linked to oil supply flows and refinery operations.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I'm going to tell the truth': Netanyahu hits back at Mamdani ahead of UN speech
articles.summary: Middle East News: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday he would use his address to the United Nations this week to defend Israel's military actions.
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday he would use his address to the United Nations this week to defend Israel's military actions against Palestinians. Hitting out at the New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, he also accused him of supporting Hamas.Netanyahu is due to address the UN general assembly on Thursday. His remarks came after Mamdani, speaking to CNN on Monday, described Netanyahu as a "war criminal and an architect of a horrific genocide of the Palestinian people"."I'm coming to the UN," Netanyahu said in a brief video statement. "I'm going to tell the truth about our heroic soldiers, and I'm going to tell the truth about you (Mamdani)."Netanyahu hits out at MamdaniNetanyahu also accused Mamdani of supporting Hamas and inciting unrest against Jewish people in New York."Shame on you, Mr Mamdani," Netanyahu said. "Shame on you for supporting the Hamas terrorist monsters who butchered our people. Shame on you for inciting riots against New York Jews."Mamdani has previously said he would arrest Netanyahu, but later acknowledged that he did not have the power to do so.Some Republican opponents have accused Mamdani of antisemitism over his pro-Palestinian advocacy and criticism of Israel's military actions in Gaza. Mamdani has condemned antisemitism and said his criticism of Israel is wrongly conflated with antisemitism.Israel-Gaza warThe Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023 killed about 1,200 people and resulted in 251 others being kidnapped, according to Israeli authorities.Israel responded with an air and ground offensive that it says is aimed at dismantling Hamas' military and governing capabilities. More than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed, according to Gaza health officials, whose figures do not distinguish between fighters and non-combatants.Israel has denied committing genocide in Gaza. It says it is fighting Hamas militants and accuses the group of operating from civilian areas.Netanyahu to defend Israel at UNNetanyahu's spokesman Doron Spielman said last week that the prime minister would use the UN platform to present Israel's position."and he's going to use that platform to address the truth in a forum of countries that are often buying a false narrative about Israel," Spielman told Reuters."It's one of the most important stages for the Prime Minister of Israel to stand on and present the truth to the world. That's our goal. He's not intimidated by anybody. He's not intimidated by Mayor Mamdani," he said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gurugram collapses in rains while Greater Noida planned for 30-40 years: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said the urban system in Gurugram collapses during rains because adequate investment was not made in infrastru.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said the urban system in Gurugram collapses during rains because adequate investment was not made in infrastructure such as drainage and sewage systems. The court contrasted this with Greater Noida, saying the latter was planned with the next 30-40 years in mind.The observations came while the top court was hearing a plea challenging the Karnataka High Court's decision upholding the state's Premium Floor Area Ratio (FAR) scheme.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, issued notice on the plea filed by the Citizens Action Forum.The bench, however, clarified that the additional FAR available under the scheme should not be used to regularise illegal construction.Supreme Court raises infrastructure concernsChief Justice Surya Kant said there was no visible improvement or addition to the basic infrastructure of the township, such as roads, sewer lines and bus flyovers, despite the additional construction capacity."We have seen in Gurugram how this system collapses if any natural calamity comes. Because, without adding to this infrastructure, you are burdening the size of the plot with multiple storeys," the CJI said.He said the situation was different in Greater Noida because the city had been planned keeping the next 30-40 years in mind.The observations came amid arguments over whether Bengaluru's existing infrastructure can support additional construction allowed under the Premium FAR scheme.What is the Premium FAR scheme?The Premium FAR scheme allows property owners to purchase additional construction rights beyond the ordinarily permissible FAR by paying prescribed premium charges. The stated objective is to facilitate vertical development and generate revenue for urban local bodies.FAR refers to the ratio of a building's total floor area to the size of the plot on which it stands.Senior advocate Aditya Sondhi, appearing for the Citizens Action Forum, argued that road width had effectively become the main criterion for granting Premium FAR, despite existing pressure on Bengaluru's parking, water, electricity and other infrastructure.Justice Bagchi also referred to Bengaluru's traffic problems, saying the city has a "traffic nightmare" and that this was a serious concern raised by the petitioner.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the state authorities, said the overall additional FAR remained capped at 0.6. He also said existing setback and parking requirements continued to apply and that developers could not simply purchase additional FAR without meeting parking and other regulatory requirements.Mehta said the money collected under the scheme would go into a dedicated fund for civic infrastructure.Government says Premium FAR cannot regularise illegal buildingsA key issue before the bench was whether the Premium FAR scheme could be used to regularise unauthorised construction.Sondhi questioned how the new scheme differed from the earlier Akrama-Sakrama scheme, under which unauthorised constructions were legalised. He told the court that a provision in the Greater Bengaluru Authority Act allowed Premium FAR to be used for regularising existing illegal constructions.Mehta rejected the contention and gave an assurance that unauthorised construction covered by the Akrama-Sakrama scheme would not be regularised under the Premium FAR scheme."It has nothing to do with that. Kindly record my statement. It is completely different. You can also pass directions to this effect," Mehta said.He argued that urban space was limited and vertical growth was the way forward, adding that cities were increasingly moving towards vertical development.Karnataka authorities get four weeks to respondThe Supreme Court asked the Bengaluru authorities to file their response to the plea within four weeks.The case challenges the Karnataka High Court's June 15 judgment upholding the constitutional validity of the Premium FAR scheme. The high court had dismissed petitions arguing that the scheme violated property rights and reduced the value of Transferable Development Rights (TDRs).The Premium FAR scheme was introduced under Section 18-B of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961. The high court had held that it did not violate Articles 14, 21 or 300A of the Constitution.The NGO had argued that Premium FAR allowed developers to purchase additional building rights at rates significantly below the market cost of TDRs, thereby undermining TDRs secured by landowners as compensation for land.The high court rejected the argument, holding that a state policy resulting in fluctuations in property values would not by itself make the policy violative of Article 300A.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of deadly strikes as thousands flee
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthis accused Saudi Arabia on Tuesday of launching a wave of deadly strikes that killed civilians and prison inmates, as Riyadh seeks to repel an o...
articles.body:
Yemen's Houthis accused Saudi Arabia on Tuesday of launching a wave of deadly strikes that killed civilians and prison inmates, as Riyadh seeks to repel an offensive that has seen the Iran-backed group seize strategic territory.

The recent Houthi takeover of Yemen's Red Sea coast has left hundreds dead and heightened fears over global trade and shipping through the vital Bab al-Mandab strait.

It has also forced thousands to flee, with the United Nations on Tuesday forecasting the number of displaced could swell from over 130,000 today to more than 230,000 in the coming months.

The gains made by the Houthis have cemented the hold of Iran and its regional allies over two key waterways in the Middle East -- and the straits of Bab al-Mandab and Hormuz -- which are major shipping arteries for global flows of energy.

Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's internationally-recognised government, has sought to contain the Houthi advance with airstrikes.

The Houthis have retaliated with attacks on Saudi territory, including a strike targeting the capital Riyadh for the first time in years.

The strike came days after Saudi Arabia accused the Houthis of targeting the holy city of Mecca, though the fighters denied the claim.

In a rare statement, Saudi King Salman praised the armed forces and security services for defending the country, and condemned the alleged attempt to target Mecca, calling it "a provocation to Muslims around the world", and branded the Houthis a "terrorist militia".

In Yemen, the Houthis said a strike on a prison killed nine detainees, while they also accused the Saudis of killing six civilians including two children in the port city of Mocha.

Two more civilians were killed by strikes in Yemen's Al-Jawf province, the Houthis added.

"A mother and child were killed, while her husband and two of her other children were wounded in strikes carried out by the Saudi enemy" in the Al-Batin area, Houthi media said, citing the Houthi health ministry.

As violence has escalated, thousands of families have been forced from their homes, many for a second or third time.

"I hope I can find a house to live in with my children. We're exhausted by the heat, the dust and the humiliation," Arwa, a mother of four children, told AFP at a camp for displaced people near Aden.

The Middle East war began in February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which prompted the Islamic republic to retaliate with attacks around the region and by mobilising its allies.

While the Yemen civil war predates the broader regional conflict, it has become its most active front in recent days.

Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces has in the past two days killed 154 people, military sources from both sides told AFP.

"The death toll from Saudi airstrikes, clashes and artillery fire in the governorates of Taiz, Al-Jawf, Marib and Saada stands at 118," Houthi military sources said, while government sources reported 36 killed in their ranks.

Saudi Arabia's civil defence agency on Tuesday issued a warning of potential danger in the country's south near the Yemen border, the first alert since the Houthis launched their attack on Riyadh over the weekend.

The alert, which asked people to remain indoors and avoid open areas, was lifted a short while later.

G7 leaders representing Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States called on the Houthis to "immediately cease all military actions".

They also demanded the Houthis end "all threats and attacks against civilian shipping, and to return to the political process in good faith", while urging Tehran "to end its arming of and support for the Houthis".

Britain has agreed to provide some military support to Saudi Arabia, defence minister Luke Pollard said, while France also pledged to help secure Saudi energy infrastructure, a diplomatic source told AFP.

But "this in no way involves taking part in the conflict with the Houthis", the French source said.

The Houthis have carried out attacks against facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in the Red Sea port city of Yanbu.

Yemen's government and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman have reportedly requested help from US President Donald Trump in fighting the Houthis.

On Tuesday in New York, Trump was due to meet with leaders of the Gulf Cooperation Council on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

The GCC, in which Saudi Arabia plays an outsized role, has in the past urged Trump against further escalation in the war with Iran.

articles.title: Idaho teacher, 67, retires and moves to Delaware to care for her grandchild after childcare costs matched the mortgage; now she spends 30 hours a week caring for the baby as US childcare costs soar
articles.summary: US News: Mary Jo Galusha, 67, a school teacher from Idaho, had a clear picture of how her retirement would look. Quiet mornings, self-care, reading time, and m.
articles.body: Mary Jo Galusha, 67, a school teacher from Idaho, had a clear picture of how her retirement would look. Quiet mornings, self-care, reading time, and maybe a little gardening. Then her daughter, Stacia Bourne, called with news. Bourne’s first child’s daycare bill nearly matched the family mortgage. Bourne and her husband even hesitated to have a second child. But that ended in a question: could they actually afford a second baby?"We were thinking we couldn't afford it," Bourne, a University of Delaware psychology professor who lives in Maryland, told NPR. So, Galusha decided to help. She now looks after her grandchildren. Her retirement plan looks more than perfect. And for the couple, this decision is nothing short of a blessing.Leaving Idaho for grandkidsStacia Bourne and her husband had their first child, George, in 2020. He started daycare when he was 2, but the cost wasn’t something they expected. "The cost for childcare for him is about the same as our mortgage," Bourne said.They were worried about whether they could afford a second child. That’s when Bourne’s mum, Mary Jo Galusha, offered: she could retire and relocate to the East Coast if Bourne was planning to have another baby. Many months later, the phone rang again. "I got a call that Stacia was expecting and that I better start planning on retiring," Galusha recalled. She gave notice, traded her Volkswagen Beetle for an SUV with enough room for car seats, and drove across the country to Newark, Delaware. Robin, the second child, was born in late 2024, and Galusha spends 30 hours a week taking care of the baby while the couple goes to work.For Galusha, though, it’s not a chore. If anything, caring for her grandchildren brings her joy. "It's like magic to watch them grow up," she told the broadcaster.Rising childcare costs in the USGrandparents caring for their grandchildren is nothing new. However, the astronomical spike in childcare costs in the US has made this crucial for many parents.Childcare for children under five in the US costs an average of $13,184 a year in 2025, according to the group Child Care Aware of America. In some places, it can cost as much as rent or college tuition.Families who cannot afford childcare or find a place at a daycare are increasingly turning to grandparents for help, according to Nicole Jorwic of Caring Across Generations. "The reality is that because this country hasn't invested in a childcare infrastructure that is flexible and affordable and reliable, grandparents are filling in the gaps that the service system leaves behind," she told the outlet.For many families in the US, finding reliable childcare has become increasingly important, says Madonna Harrington Meyer, a Syracuse University sociology professor who studies ageing and grandparenting. In recent decades, the number of households with both parents working full-time has risen. In 2025, 52% of couples with children had both parents working full-time, up from 31% in 1975, according to Pew Research Center.There has also been a steady increase in the number of single mums in the US over the course of decades. Families of children with disabilities also struggle to find specialised care. "All of these things are reasons people turn to grandparents," Harrington Meyer said.And most grandparents are happy to help. According to a 2024 poll, nearly half of grandparents with grandchildren under 18 cared for them at least once every few months.Another AARP report found that grandparents mainly provide childcare because their children are working or busy, and they want to spend more time with their grandchildren. The median amount of time they spend providing care is 200 hours a year, or about 3.8 hours a week."But perhaps the biggest benefit is that they are so flexible. Unlike a formal daycare situation, often grandparents will come to your house, or they'll alternate between watching the children at their own house and at the grandparent's house," Harrington Meyer added.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Indian Railways is preparing to add another Sleeper Vande Bharat service to one of the country's busiest travel corridors. According to a recent Times of India report, a second Sleeper Vande Bharat is being planned between Delhi and Varanasi. As per reports, the train will pass through Kanpur and Prayagraj, potentially giving travellers a new overnight option between the national capital and Uttar Pradesh's major cultural destinations. The Vande Bharat Sleeper is designed to make long-distance rail travel more comfortable for passengers.The Railway Ministry in April 2026 said that the New Delhi–Varanasi route had already carried more than 73 lakh passengers, making it the busiest Vande Bharat route.Let’s find out more about this new upcoming train service:A convenient and modern overnight Delhi–Varanasi optionAccording to the proposed schedule reported by railway officials, the train would leave Varanasi Cantt at around 9:20 PM and reach Prayagraj at approximately 10:45 PM. It would then pass through Kanpur Central around 12:35 AM, before reaching New Delhi at about 5 AM.In the opposite direction, the proposed train would depart New Delhi at around 9:20 PM and reach Varanasi at 5 AM the following morningHowever, these timings are proposed rather than final. The Railway Board has not yet announced the confirmed timetable, train number, fare or date.A 16-coach train with three classesThe proposed Delhi–Varanasi service is expected to use a 16-coach Sleeper Vande Bharat, according to reports. The train will feature:11 AC 3-tier coachesFour AC 2-tier coachesOne First AC coachCapacity: 823 passengersThe Sleeper Vande Bharat itself has been developed as a fully air-conditioned train, with ergonomically designed berths intended to make overnight travel easier. The Railway Ministry has specifically highlighted the ergonomically designed ladder for upper berthsAccording to government’s official website, the sleeper coaches feature:Jerk-Free Semi permanent couplers and Anti Climbers.KAVACH for added securityOperating speed of 160 km/hr to 180 km/hr highest.Fire barrier doorsCentrally controlled Automatic Plug DoorsCCTVs in all coaches.Emergency talk-back unitFor Divyangjan passengers, a special lavatory in the driving coaches on each end.Ergonomically designed ladder for ease of climbing onto upper berths.InteriorsThe interiors are among the biggest changes. The Railway Ministry says the Sleeper Vande Bharat is equipped with modern toilets, while its coaches incorporate systems aimed at improving hygiene and passenger comfort. There are also CCTV cameras in all coaches, another best feature of the train.For now, the key attraction is not simply about travelling faster. articles.title: Xi-Trump summit: China puts Taiwan ‘red line’ at centre of US ties
articles.summary: China News: China on Tuesday again warned that Taiwan remains a “red line” in its ties with the United States, just a day before Chinese President Xi Jinping is d.
articles.body: China on Tuesday again warned that Taiwan remains a “red line” in its ties with the United States, just a day before Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to travel to Washington for a summit with US President Donald Trump. Beijing's warning came as the two leaders prepare to discuss a relationship marked by tensions over Taiwan, trade and security.Xi is scheduled to meet Trump on Thursday during his three-day visit to Washington. It will be their second meeting since May. Beijing has described the summit, coming less than six months after their previous meeting, as a "milestone of historic significance".Taiwan at centre of US-China tiesAhead of Xi's visit, Chinese state media People's Daily put Taiwan at the centre of the US-China relationship.A front-page article described Taiwan as a "red line” for Beijing and called it a guardrail and safety net for China-US relations, the Hong Kong-based South China Morning Post reported.“Managing ‘Taiwan independence’ is a key part of building constructive strategic stability between China and the US,” the article said, describing pro-independence forces as a “common enemy” of Beijing and Washington."The US side must handle the Taiwan question with the utmost caution and take concrete action to safeguard the stable development of China-US relations and peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait,” it warned.Xi is widely expected to raise Beijing's opposition to a proposed US arms package worth about USD 11 billion for Taiwan. Trump has yet to approve the package. China is also expected to press Washington to scale back its support for Taipei.Beijing claims Taiwan as part of its territory and has vowed to achieve integration with the island. It also opposes countries with which it has diplomatic relations maintaining formal ties with Taipei.Japan factorChina is also watching Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's meeting with Trump in New York on Tuesday.Takaichi is expected to stress the strength of the US-Japan alliance and the need to maintain a strong position on Taiwan, Japanese officials said. Her meeting with Trump comes as Tokyo seeks to coordinate with Washington on China ahead of Xi's visit.Japanese officials said Takaichi would also emphasise the need to strengthen deterrence against what Tokyo describes as Chinese military and economic coercion, the Japan Times reported.Relations between China and Japan have remained tense since November last year, when Takaichi said in parliament that a Taiwan contingency could become a "survival-threatening situation" for Japan and potentially lead to action by its defence forces in support of the US.Her remarks angered Beijing, which considers Taiwan part of its territory.Beijing signals focus on stabilityAhead of Xi's visit, Chaoyang Shaoxia, a social-media channel widely believed to be affiliated with China's foreign ministry, said the trip was aimed at “keeping the positive momentum going”.The Chinese foreign ministry, its embassies and ambassadors also posted videos in Chinese and English saying that “from Beijing to Washington DC, the China-US relationship must stay on course towards constructive strategic stability”.Asked about the posts, foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday, “China is ready to work with the US to enrich the China-US constructive relationship of strategic stability, enhance dialogue and cooperation, and properly manage differences to contribute to the well-being of both peoples and to a peaceful, stable and prosperous world”.Fentanyl curbsChina also announced tighter controls on the export of chemicals that can be diverted into the production of fentanyl, addressing another long-standing US demand.Chinese anti-narcotics authorities warned companies and individuals to prevent medetomidine and tartaric acid from being diverted into narcotics production.The China national narcotics control commission said the move was part of intensified efforts to stop chemicals with potential uses in illegal drug production from reaching illicit channels, state-run Xinhua news agency reported.Trump has repeatedly pressed Beijing to curb the supply of chemicals and equipment used to manufacture fentanyl, a powerful synthetic opioid linked to the widespread drug addiction crisis in the US.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A man searching for pigeon rings in Romania found a 4,000-year-old hoard of gold ornaments and copper axes
articles.summary: UK News: A man searching for homing pigeon rings with a metal detector in Romania accidentally uncovered a prehistoric hoard containing copper axes and gold or.
articles.body: A man searching for homing pigeon rings with a metal detector in Romania accidentally uncovered a prehistoric hoard containing copper axes and gold ornaments. Found at the base of a tree in Cocoșești commune, Prahova County, on 20 July 2020, the hoard was buried about 0.30 metres below the surface. It contained two copper shaft-hole axes, three chained gold hair-rings and a string of 54 gold beads. Archaeologists later recovered nine additional gold beads from the surrounding soil during an investigation of the site. Researchers examining the objects concluded that the hoarding most likely took place in the late third millennium BC.How did a pigeon-ring search uncover a 4,000-year-old hoardAccording to the study published in Springer Nature Link, titled ‘From chance to understanding: Scientific investigations of a prehistoric hoard from Southern Romania (Cocoșești, Prahova)’, the material analysed from the Cocoșești hoard consisted of two copper shaft-hole axes, three chained gold hair-rings and a string containing 54 gold beads. The researchers initially examined the objects macroscopically before carrying out further archaeological and scientific investigations. The combination brought together copper weapons or tools and gold ornaments within the same deposit.The archaeological investigation also helped reconstruct the arrangement of the objects. The axes had been placed next to one another on their wide, level sides, oriented north-south, while the gold hair-rings and bead string had been positioned above them. Because the gold ornaments had been incompletely recovered by the finder, their exact original positioning could not be fully observed. Researchers excavated and examined the area around the original hole and found no evidence of human interference dating to the period when the hoard was deposited.Researchers recovered nine gold beads from the discovery areaThe researchers returned to the discovery area with metal-detecting equipment as part of their archaeological investigation. Three gold beads were recovered from soil that had already been removed by the discoverer. More than 50 kilograms of additional soil from the area were then removed and sieved while being examined with a hand-held detector. This process produced six more gold beads.The additional recovery helped researchers confirm the reported find location and contributed to reconstructing the hoard’s original arrangement. The objects were also subjected to non-invasive scientific analysis. X-ray fluorescence analysis was used to examine their elemental composition, while the wider investigation considered the archaeological context, raw materials, manufacturing technology and traces of wear on the objects.The copper axes may be the hoard’s earliest objectsThe two copper axes appear to be the earliest objects in the hoard. Their form and characteristics have parallels among axes associated with the middle of the third millennium BC. The researchers also note that the axes were made of copper with a low arsenic content, a feature associated with shaft-hole axes from earlier periods of the Bronze Age.The gold hair-rings and beads are considered later additions based on their parallels and metal composition. The researchers conclude that the hoarding act most likely occurred in the late third millennium BC. The combination of shaft-hole axes with ornaments, and copper with gold, is rare in the Carpathian-Danube region during the third millennium BC.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Shriyan Avadhanula, the 16-year-old Virginia student who built a free college-prep platform after getting frustrated by paid resources; Scholark has crossed 10,000 users
articles.summary: US News: College applications involve more than just writing essays; they also demand that students scour through a thousand websites in need of information, p.
articles.body: College applications involve more than just writing essays; they also demand that students scour through a thousand websites in need of information, process it on their own and spend an enormous amount of time, doing everything rather than applying. Frustrated with the scattered, costly resources for college preparation, a 16-year-old high school student in Virginia saw an opportunity to help others like him out.Shriyan Avadhanula was juggling his IB coursework, varsity soccer, and competitive pickleball while also being a junior at Henrico High School in Virginia. At the same time, he was navigating college websites, GPA calculators, SAT resources and test preparation platforms. According to him, the information he wanted usually existed, but it was scattered across different websites, sometimes difficult to interpret and often behind paywalls.“I used to have a bunch of tabs up on my computer, where it's like a GPA calculator, college websites, SAT resources — all of that stuff was so overwhelming,” he said.Eventually, during his freshman year, he decided to see if he could build a better alternative himself. What he began as a basic GPA calculator and college admissions prediction tool, eventually became Scholark, a free digital platform that now includes AP test preparation and college admissions resources. Avadhanula estimated he spent roughly two and a half to three years building and revising it, adding features as he encountered new needs as a student himself.It wasn't that information was not available about college; but Avadhanula said that it was presented in a disjointed way and still students like him were trying to use it. “Why not just build a platform ... I can use with everyone else?” he recalled thinking.College websites can present students with statistics, admissions requirements and other information within what Avadhanula described as a “big wall of text.” With Scholark — which Avadhanula noted ends with a ‘K’ for visually aesthetic purposes- he sought to organise information around the questions and resources he and other students were looking for.Another consideration was the cost. While preparing for his AP Computer Science Principles exam, Avadhanula recalled completing roughly 50 practice questions through an online resource before encountering a prompt asking him to pay $49.99 for a subscription to see his score. “That really, really annoyed me and frustrated me,” he said. “And I realised that wasn't the only place that does it.” Moreover, he said that experience reinforced his desire to keep Scholark free.The platform’s earliest iteration was much simpler than it is today, with a GPA calculator and an AP study guide component he initially built to help himself prepare for AP Computer Science Principles with better practice materials. Learning some of the technical skills needed to build it through online programs and from his father, who works in software development, Avadhanula said he built Scholark using website tools like HTML, CSS and, primarily, JavaScript. As the project progressed, he also began using artificial intelligence to help identify bugs in thousands of lines of code.“I remember spending countless nights, no sleep, just trying to learn how [the College Board] make their questions," he said. “And then I learned. I made, I think, 50 questions on how they phrase it, and then trained my AI agent to continue making questions like that the way I did it, and that's where it started making them more accurate.” The process paid off for him personally, Avadhanula said he used the early version of the platform to study for the aforementioned AP Computer Science Principles exam and earned a four out of five.From there, Avadhanula said Scholark kept growing, adding more college-planning resources, including an admissions prediction feature that compares information students enter with publicly available admissions data.That feature grew out of another problem he encountered as a user, different admissions websites could give substantially different predictions, without always making it clear where those estimates came from. Scholark shows users the data behind its estimates, he said, though he is careful not to present the results as definitive. “I'm not going to claim that it's 100 per cent accurate because I don't believe anything is 100 per cent accurate, because there's always room to grow,” he said.Avadhanula shared Scholark with friends, asked them to be candid about what worked and what didn't, and continued making changes based on their feedback. But then people he didn't know started finding and using it. Avadhanula said more than 10,000 users have accessed Scholark since its launch in 2025, with traffic peaking around AP exam season as students searched for free study resources. Seeing that growth was unexpected, he said, particularly for something that began as a tool he had built for himself. “I didn't think people would actually use it,” he said.Now, those users give him another reason to keep tinkering with a platform he still considers a work in progress, but the perspective that prompted him to start building it hasn't changed: He is still one of the students trying to navigate the information Scholark was designed to curate.“I made the whole UI [user interface] itself very easy to access, very student-like, because I'm a student as well,” Avadhanula said. “I know what a student wants to see.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2018, Welsh adventurer Ash Dykes walked 4,000 miles along China's Yangtze; 352 days, 8 million steps, wolves and bears later, he reached Shanghai
articles.summary: UK News: British adventurer Ash Dykes became the first person to walk the length of China's Yangtze River, covering 6,437 kilometres, or about 4,000 miles, fro.
articles.body: British adventurer Ash Dykes became the first person to walk the length of China's Yangtze River, covering 6,437 kilometres, or about 4,000 miles, from the river's scientific source in southern Qinghai to its mouth near Shanghai. Guinness World Records officially recognised the feat after Dykes began his expedition on August 26, 2018, and completed it 352 days later on August 12, 2019. Guinness estimates that the journey involved roughly 8 million steps. Starting on the Tibetan Plateau at an altitude of more than 5,000 metres, Dykes travelled through some of China's most remote landscapes before reaching the densely populated lower reaches of the Yangtze. Along the way, he encountered sub-zero temperatures, difficult valleys and wild animals including wolves and bears, while also receiving support from people he met in communities along the route. The expedition became Dykes's third world-first record.Two years of preparation went into the attemptDykes spent 2 years preparing for the expedition before setting out. His official Mission Yangtze material described the journey as a year-long attempt to cover the 6,437-kilometre route on foot, with the expedition requiring extensive physical training, logistics and preparation for rapidly changing conditions. The journey began at what Dykes described as the scientific source of the Yangtze in southern Qinghai on the Tibetan Plateau. His expedition records place the starting point at more than 5,000 metres above sea level, meaning the early stages involved high-altitude conditions and sub-zero temperatures.The terrain presented another challenge. Dykes's preparations accounted for isolation, difficult valleys, forests and major changes in climate as he travelled from the river's headwaters towards eastern China. His expedition material also warned that he could encounter wildlife including snakes, bears, wolves and Asian giant hornets. By November 2018, after 11 weeks on the route, Dykes had covered about 1,500 miles and travelled through Qinghai, Sichuan and into Yunnan. He was gradually descending from the high-altitude headwaters as the landscape and climate changed around him.The route took him from remote mountains to the Three GorgesDykes's journey followed the Yangtze from its scientific source towards the East China Sea, taking him through dramatically different environments as the river grew from a high-altitude waterway into one of China's major rivers. One of the landmarks he encountered was the Qutang Gorge, the first of the Yangtze's Three Gorges. Dykes described it as the shortest of the 3 gorges and noted that the river narrows to about 150 metres between mountains reaching around 1,200 metres. The expedition also took him through areas with deep historical and cultural significance. Guinness notes that archaeological sites dating back thousands of years have been found around the Yangtze and that the river has played a major role in the development of Chinese civilisation.As Dykes moved further east, the contrast with the isolated headwaters became increasingly pronounced. His expedition records describe a progression from remote rural areas and difficult terrain towards forests, historic cities and densely populated urban landscapes. The Yangtze itself is the longest river in the world to flow entirely through a single country. Its source is on the Tibetan Plateau, often described as the “roof of the world”, while the river eventually reaches the East China Sea near Shanghai.Wildlife and isolation were among the expedition's challengesThe first half of the journey was particularly demanding because much of the route passed through sparsely populated, high-altitude and remote areas. Dykes documented encounters and close proximity to wildlife during the expedition, including bears, wolves, wild yak and other animals. Guinness described the journey as involving sub-zero temperatures, wolves, bears and treacherous valleys. Dykes's own expedition updates also recorded camping in bear country and dealing with wild yak during the early stages.The physical challenges were accompanied by the logistical demands of maintaining a long-distance expedition over nearly a year. Dykes had to travel through changing climates while continuing to cover hundreds of kilometres at a time. His expedition website later described the journey as involving more than 8 million steps. The expedition was not entirely solitary, however. Dykes received support from people he encountered across China, with locals joining him for portions of his hikes, inviting him into their homes and helping him along the way. Guinness reported that this hospitality became an important part of his experience of the country.The Yangtze expedition ended with a third world-firstAfter 352 days on the route, Dykes reached the Yangtze's mouth near Shanghai on August 12, 2019. Guinness World Records lists him as the first person to walk the length of the Yangtze River, with the record covering 6,437 kilometres from southern Qinghai to Shanghai. The expedition became Dykes's third world-first record. He had previously completed long-distance expeditions across Mongolia and Madagascar, including a 1,600-mile traverse of Madagascar's interior in 2016.Reflecting on the Yangtze journey after completing it, Dykes described it as both a physical and cultural experience. He credited the people he met across rural and urban China for the hospitality and support he received during the expedition. The journey also became a record of the dramatic geographical transition along the Yangtze, beginning with a river at more than 5,000 metres above sea level on the Tibetan Plateau and ending nearly 4,000 miles later at its mouth near Shanghai.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1993, buyers paid $490,000 for Kurt Weill’s former 5.5-acre New York estate; after 33 years of restoration, the 1880 property is now asking $1.995 million
articles.summary: Real Estate News: A 5.5-acre historic country estate in New City, New York, once home to famous German composer Kurt Weill and actress Lotte Lenya, is now for sale for .
articles.body: A 5.5-acre historic country estate in New City, New York, once home to famous German composer Kurt Weill and actress Lotte Lenya, is now for sale for $1.995 million. Known as Brook House, the property at 116 South Mountain Road was bought by its current owners in 1993 for $490,000. Over the last 33 years, the owners have worked on a major restoration to update the 1880 home while keeping its rich creative history intact. Listed by property brokerage Ellis Sotheby's International Realty, the estate first went on the market earlier this year for $2.295 million before the price was lowered by $300,000 in September.A historic refuge for world-renowned creatorsAccording to real estate records published on Realtor.com and Zillow, Brook House has had only four owners in the last 110 years. It was inside this stone house that Kurt Weill and his wife, singer and actress Lotte Lenya, lived for more than three decades. While living there, Weill wrote famous theater songs, including "Mack the Knife" and "Alabama Song" from The Threepenny Opera. Before Weill and Lenya, the home belonged to Rollo Peters, a well known American stage actor, director, and co-founder of the Theatre Guild. The estate sits within the historic South Mountain Road area, an artists' community in Rockland County once home to notable cultural figures such as playwright Maxwell Anderson, sculptor John Mowbray-Clark, and painter Arthur B. Davies. Listing agent Richard Ellis of Ellis Sotheby's International Realty spoke about the home's appeal in property marketing materials. "Brook House offers a once-in-a-generation opportunity to own a residence where architecture, landscape and cultural history converge in one of the Northeast's most quietly legendary artist communities," Ellis said. "The result is a rare blend of historic authenticity, wonderful provenance, artistic legacy and refined country design."Architectural details and comprehensive restorationThe main colonial-style home spans about 4,600 square feet and blends traditional 19th-century craftsmanship with modern structural updates. Inside, the home has old hand-cut wooden beams, exposed stone walls, and four wood-burning fireplaces with period mantels, including one from the 19th century and a Louis XV-style French limestone design. The living room has tall ceilings, wide white oak floors, tray ceilings, and French doors that open out to the grounds. To finish the interior restoration, the current owners worked with New York-based interior designer Gail Jacobs. Jacobs, known for her work on high-profile historic homes including Leonard Bernstein's former apartment at The Dakota in Manhattan, helped find period-appropriate fixtures such as antique Holophane-style lighting and Ann-Morris decorative pieces. In total, the estate has five bedrooms and three and a half bathrooms across the main house and other buildings on the property.Private grounds and legal two-family zoningThe property is officially zoned as a legal two-family home, with a separate guest house that has its own living room fireplace, full kitchen, two bedrooms, one and a half bathrooms, and a walk-out lower-level den. Other structures on the 5.5-acre property include an oversized garage now used as a workshop, an old brick potting shed, a large garden shed, and a chicken coop. A private well continually supplies water to the grounds. The natural landscape is designed like a private arboretum, with flowering gardens, rolling fields, and original dry-stone walls. The West Branch of the Hackensack River runs directly through the property, crossed by a rebuilt stone arch bridge. To help protect the land around it, Lotte Lenya once donated eight acres of neighboring land to the West Branch Conservation Land Trust. Today, Brook House borders the 91-acre Davenport Preserve, keeping the estate surrounded by protected woodland. Tax records listed on Realtor.com show the estimated annual property tax for the estate is $25,979.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: England released its first 6 white-tailed eagles in 2019 after a 240-year absence; by 2026, the project had produced 9 wild-born chicks, including 3 this summer
articles.summary: UK News: For centuries, white-tailed eagles were part of England’s landscape. Then persecution drove them out, leaving the country without its largest bird of .
articles.body: For centuries, white-tailed eagles were part of England’s landscape. Then persecution drove them out, leaving the country without its largest bird of prey for generations. Now, almost a quarter of a century after the species disappeared from English skies, a carefully managed reintroduction is beginning to reshape that story, states an online report by Forestry England. Three more chicks have fledged this summer, taking the number of wild-born young produced through the project to nine, adds the report. Scroll down to read the details of the change.Three new eagles take flightThe latest breeding success came from two established pairs descended from birds released as part of the reintroduction programme run by Forestry England and the Roy Dennis Wildlife Foundation, states the online report.Two male chicks hatched in Sussex, becoming the latest offspring of a pair that has successfully bred every year since 2023. Their parents were among the white-tailed eagles released in England in 2020 and have now become one of the project's established breeding pairs, the report states. A third male chick fledged from a nest in Dorset. The breeding pair has now successfully raised young for a second time. The achievement is particularly notable because the male adult has survived despite having only one leg, which he lost five years ago.As per the report, the three chicks were fitted with satellite tags, allowing conservation teams to follow their movements as they begin exploring the wider British landscape.A species returns after 240 yearsWhite-tailed eagles are Britain's largest birds of prey, with wingspans reaching around 2.5 metres. Once widespread across England, the species was driven to extinction in the country through human persecution. The last pair is recorded as having bred in southern England in 1780, adds the online report.The modern reintroduction effort began in 2019, when the first six birds were released. Since then, 56 young white-tailed eagles have been released into the English landscape. Five pairs from the project have now formed established bonds, with two successfully producing chicks this year. Three additional pairs are also well established, offering the prospect of further breeding activity in coming seasons.Tracking what the eagles eatSatellite monitoring has become an important part of understanding how the reintroduced birds are adapting. Data from previous fledglings has shown the young eagles travelling widely across the UK as they establish their own territories.This year, researchers also gained a closer look at what the breeding birds were feeding their young. Specialist cameras positioned near the nests recorded more than 300 instances of food being brought to the chicks. Fish dominated the menu, reflecting the species' close association with wetlands, rivers and coastal environments, explains the online report.Expanding the reintroductionThe programme is continuing to grow. Five young eagles were released this summer from the project's base on the Isle of Wight, while six additional birds were released at Exmoor National Park for the first time, in partnership with the Exmoor National Park Authority. The releases are carried out under licence from Natural England, while birds destined for reintroduction are collected from wild nests in Scotland under licence from NatureScot, adds the online report by Forestry England.For a species absent from England for more than two centuries, the sight of wild-born chicks taking their first flights represents a significant shift. With established pairs now raising young of their own, the white-tailed eagle's return is moving beyond a release programme and toward a self-sustaining presence in England's skies.Image Courtesy: Forestry EnglandCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: An Illinois thrift store has collected more than 100,000 donated items and runs with 200 regular volunteers, using every resale purchase to support local families in crisis
articles.summary: US News: An Illinois thrift shop run by a team of 200 regular volunteers has processed more than 100,000 donated items, putting every dollar earned from second.
articles.body: An Illinois thrift shop run by a team of 200 regular volunteers has processed more than 100,000 donated items, putting every dollar earned from second-hand sales toward helping local families going through financial hardship. House of Hope Resale, located in Barrington, Illinois, turns unwanted household goods, clothing, and furniture into direct emergency help. Run under Project Hope of Barrington, the thrift store funds emergency assistance programs for local residents facing sudden hardship, job loss, medical emergencies, or housing problems. According to event details published on the official House of Hope Resale website, the non-profit store depends on a large community network to sort, display, and sell donated items. The money made at checkout goes straight into emergency relief funds, turning everyday purchases into direct help for the community.Community support through volunteer workThis large operation runs thanks to a dedicated team of unpaid helpers. Official event listings from the organization show that around 200 regular volunteers staff the store floor, handle intake, sort donations, and prepare items for sale all year long. To keep staffing steady and bring in new helpers, the shop regularly hosts recruitment events and community gatherings. Announcements on the House of Hope website mentioned a "Volunteer Pop-Up" event held in September 2026, meant to introduce local residents to different roles at the shop, along with regular "Meet and Greet" sessions for people interested in volunteering. These recruitment events help new volunteers understand how processing donated goods directly funds local safety nets. Volunteers help with everything from setting up merchandise and serving customers to checking donations, making sure items move smoothly from drop-off to the store shelves.Funding emergency help for local familiesEvery purchase made at the shop directly funds Project Hope of Barrington's outreach services. The parent charity gives financial help to families within the local school district who can't afford essential living costs. According to public information from Project Hope, money raised by the resale shop covers important expenses like rent, utility bills, prescription medicine, and food assistance. Rather than working purely as a second-hand store, the shop serves as the main source of income for the charity's emergency grants. When local residents face sudden financial trouble due to illness, unexpected job loss, or a family crisis, the charity steps in with short-term financial grants. By funding these programs through retail sales, the organization helps prevent homelessness and utility shutoffs among families in need.Processing thousands of donated goodsOver its history, House of Hope Resale has collected and processed more than 100,000 donated items from residents across Barrington and nearby communities in northern Illinois. The donated items include clothing, shoes, antique furniture, kitchen appliances, home decor, books, and seasonal items. This high volume of donations requires careful sorting and quality checks to get the most value out of each item. According to event updates published by House of Hope, the constant flow of donations keeps a fresh supply of goods for bargain hunters and eco-conscious shoppers who want to keep usable items out of landfills. The store's model keeps gently used goods in circulation while raising as much money as possible for local charity work.Community events and upcoming drivesTo keep the community involved, the organization often pairs its store operations with educational events and social meetups. The House of Hope Meet and Greet events let local residents, potential volunteers, and donors meet the team, tour the processing areas, and see firsthand how donated items turn into crisis relief. By keeping a steady schedule of pop-up recruitment drives and public gatherings, the organization continues to grow its volunteer base to keep up with rising donation numbers. Interested residents are encouraged to attend information sessions or sign up for volunteer shifts through the charity's online portal. House of Hope Resale remains open to local shoppers, donors, and community members who want to support families in need across Barrington and the surrounding area.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
